corrected_content.problem:
The matrix $H$ is given below. Let ${\mathbf{h}}_{1}$, ${\mathbf{h}}_{2}$,  ${\mathbf{h}}_{3}$ and ${\mathbf{h}}_{4}$ be the respective columns of $H.$
Determine if $\mathcal{B}=\left\{{\mathbf{h}}_{1},{\mathbf{h}}_{2}\right\}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(H).$ 
If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$, where ${\mathbf{h}}_{4}={x}_{1}{\mathbf{h}}_{1}+{x}_{2}{\mathbf{h}}_{2}.$ 

$$
H=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 2 & 12 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 9 & 2\end{bmatrix}
$$
corrected_content.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $H$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}H & =\begin{bmatrix}2 & 2 & 12 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 9 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 6 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 9 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 6 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 6 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{3}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd columns. So, a basis of $\text{Col}(H)$ is $\{{\mathbf{h}}_{1},{\mathbf{h}}_{2},{\mathbf{h}}_{3}\}.$ 

Therefore, we conclude that $\mathcal{B}=\{{\mathbf{h}}_{1},{\mathbf{h}}_{2}\}$ is not a basis of $\text{Col}(H).$
